Vibhīṣaṇa brought her forth, though she was guarded by many Rākṣasas.
Approaching the high-souled one and perceiving that he was absorbed in meditation,
he bowed down with joy and announced that Sītā had been recovered.
6.102.016 Upon hearing that she had arrived after having dwelt for a long time in the house of the Rākṣasa,
three emotions— joy, dejection, and anger— overcame Rāghava.
6.102.017 Then, seeing him standing by his side, he looked at him reflectively and deliberated.
6.102.017c Unhappy, Rāghava spoke these words to Vibhīṣaṇa:
6.102.018a "O gentle lord of the rākṣasas, ever devoted to my victory,
6.102.018c let Vaidehī come quickly into my presence."
6.102.019a Having understood those words of Rāghava, Vibhīṣaṇa 6.102.019c quickly ordered efforts to clear the area on all sides.
6.102.020a There, men wearing tunics and turbans, with canes and drums in their hands, [stood ready].
6.102.020c Men moved about on all sides, driving [the crowd] away;
6.102.021a the throngs of bears, monkeys, and rākṣasas, being driven away from every direction, then retreated to a great distance.
As they were all being driven away, a roar arose from them like the sound of the ocean tossed by the wind.
Seeing them being driven out from all sides and filled with agitation, [he spoke].
Out of courtesy and because of his indignation, Rāghava restrained him.
Then Rāma, agitated and as if burning him with his eyes,
spoke these words of reproach to the highly wise Vibhīṣaṇa.
"For what reason do you disregard me and cause these people to waste away?
Turn back this exertion; these people are my own kin.
Neither houses, nor garments, nor walls can provide concealment."

6.102.026c Such honors from kings do not conceal the conduct of a woman. 6.102.027a Not in times of calamity, nor in hardships, nor in battle, nor at a *svayaṃvara*, 6.102.027c nor at a sacrifice, nor at a wedding, is the sight of a woman considered improper.
"She has entered the fray of battle and stands in great distress;
there would be no fault in her being seen, especially in my presence.
Therefore, Vibhīṣaṇa, bring her to me quickly."
"Let Sītā see me standing here, surrounded by my circle of friends.
Thus addressed by Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa, reflecting deeply,
humbly brought Sītā into Rāma’s presence.
Then Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva, and the monkey Hanumān,
having heard Rāma’s words, became deeply distressed;
for his gestures were harsh and showed no regard for his wife.
They suspected that Rāghava was as if displeased with Sītā;
meanwhile, Maithilī, shrinking back in shame from her own limbs,
approached her husband accompanied by Vibhīṣaṇa.
With her face veiled by her garment out of shame in the assembly of people,
she approached her husband and wept, calling out, "O noble son!
She lamented out of wonder, joy, and affection.
With her face even more lovely than before, she gazed at the gentle face of her husband.
Then, beholding her beloved after so long a time, she dispelled the weariness of his mind.
Her face was as lovely as the risen full moon;
at that time, her countenance resembled the stainless moon.
Then Rāma, beholding Maithilī standing by his side with a humble mien, [spoke].
With anger lodged within his heart, he began to speak:
"O blessed lady, you have been conquered by me after I had defeated my enemy in battle;
whatever was to be accomplished through manly prowess has now been achieved."
"I have reached the end of my indignation; the insult has been wiped away. Both the humiliation and the enemy have been uprooted by me simultaneously.
Today my manliness has been witnessed; today my toil has borne fruit."

6.103.004c Today, because my vow has been fulfilled, I am able to prevail here for myself. 6.103.005a You, who were carried off while separated from me by that fickle-minded Rākṣasa— 6.103.005c That fault brought about by fate has been overcome by me, a human being.
What purpose is there for that man of feeble spirit who, having encountered an insult, does not wipe it away with his own splendor? [For you,
there remains] the crossing of the ocean and the crushing of Laṅkā.
Today that praiseworthy deed of Hanumān has borne fruit;
for as he displayed his prowess in battle and offered counsel for my benefit,
the exertion of Sugrīva and his entire army has today become successful.
"Having abandoned his brother who was devoid of virtue, he has come to me of his own accord;
today the exertion of the devoted Vibhīṣaṇa has borne fruit.
As Rāma was speaking these words, Sītā [heard] that speech of his.
With eyes wide like those of a doe, she became overwhelmed with tears;
as Rāma gazed upon her, his anger flared up once more,
like a blazing fire sprinkled with abundant clarified butter.
Knitting his brows upon his face and casting sidelong glances from his eyes,
he spoke harshly to Sītā in the midst of the monkeys and rākṣasas:
"Whatever must be done by a man who seeks to wipe away an insult..."
All that was accomplished, O Sītā, by that indignant man from the hand of his enemy; for Agastya,
whose soul is purified by asceticism, has conquered the world of living beings,
just as the invincible southern quarter was subdued by the sage.
"May it be well with you; let it be known that this exhaustion from battle has been overcome through the prowess of my friends, and was not undertaken by me for your sake.
For I have acted thus in order to protect my conduct and to avoid scandal in every respect."
While wiping away the stain upon my renowned lineage,
you stand before me, casting doubt upon my conduct;
like a lamp to one with diseased eyes, you are most disagreeable to me.
6.103.018a Therefore go now, O daughter of Janaka, permitted as you wish;
6.103.018c O blessed lady, these are the ten directions [open to you]; I have no further need of you.
6.103.019a For what man born of noble lineage would [accept] a woman who has dwelt in another's house?
6.103.019c A man of spirit might take you back with a heart full of friendship;
6.103.020a but having seen you fallen from Rāvaṇa’s lap and gazed upon by his wicked eye,
6.103.020c how could I take you back again while proclaiming my great lineage?
"For that purpose you were conquered by me, and my honor has been restored. I have no attachment to you; go from here as you please.
O blessed lady, these words were spoken by me once I had made up my mind.
"O Śītā, set your mind at ease upon Lakṣmaṇa or Bharata,
or upon Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, or Vibhīṣaṇa, the lord of the Rākṣasas—
whichever brings you the greatest comfort."

"O Sītā, having seen you of divine form and enchanting beauty dwelling for long in his own home, Rāvaṇa will certainly not tolerate it. Therefore, O lady worthy of kindness, that which is unpleasant [to him]— "
Having finally heard news from her beloved, Maithilī wept most bitterly,
trembling like a creeper struck by the trunk of a lordly elephant.
6.104.001 Thus addressed with harsh words that caused her hair to stand on end by the enraged Rāghava, Vaidehī became deeply distressed.
6.104.002 For Maithilī had never before heard such words in the midst of a great assembly.

6.104.002c Having heard her husband’s harsh words, she became overcome with shame and modesty. 6.104.003a Janaka’s daughter felt as if her very limbs were shrinking within themselves; pierced by those word-arrows, as if she herself were struck by darts, she shed profuse tears.
Then, wiping her own face which was distressed by tears,
she spoke these words slowly and with a faltering voice to her husband:
"Why do you address me with such an unworthy speech, so cruel to the ears?"
"O hero, you speak harshly to me, like a common man to a common woman.
O mighty-armed one, I am not as you perceive me to be. Have confidence in me; I swear it by my own conduct."
"6.104.007a You suspect my character because of the separate conduct of women; 6.104.007c but if I have been tested by you, then you should abandon this suspicion.
6.104.008a If I, O Lord, came into contact with your body while I was helpless,"
"In that matter, it was not my own will; fate was at fault there. But as for that which is under my own control—my heart—it remains fixed upon you.
Since my limbs are subject to another's power, what can I do, being powerless?"
"O giver of honor, because we grew up together and through our constant association,
if I was not recognized by you, I am thereby destroyed forever. When the heroic Hanumān was sent by you as a scout..."
"O hero, why was I not released by you then while I was staying in Laṅkā? Immediately after your words, in the very presence of the lord of monkeys,
my life would have been abandoned by me, O hero, had I been forsaken by you."
"Let this toil of yours not be in vain, having staked your very life upon uncertainty;
nor shall this distress caused to your friends be fruitless for you. But by you, O tiger among men, who have followed only the path of wrath—"
6.104.014c By this light-minded man, womanhood alone has been placed foremost.
6.104.015a Under some pretext, he does not acknowledge his birth from the soil of Janaka;
6.104.015c And though you know my conduct, O knower of conduct, you have not held it in high regard.
"In my childhood, my hand was not taken in marriage by you, and I was tormented by you as a child. My devotion and my character—everything has been cast aside by you.
Speaking thus, she wept, her speech faltering with tears.

6.104.017c Sītā spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, who stood there dejected and lost in thought: 6.104.018a "O son of Sumitrā, prepare a funeral pyre for me; it is the remedy for this calamity. 6.104.018c Stricken by false slander, I have no desire to live."
"Since I have been abandoned by my husband in the assembly of people because he no longer finds pleasure in my virtues,
what course remains for me but to enter the fire?
Having been addressed thus by Vaidehī, Lakṣmaṇa, the slayer of enemy heroes— "
6.104.020c Overcome by indignation, he gazed upon the face of Rāghava. 6.104.021a Perceiving through his outward appearance the desire of Rāma’s mind,
the valiant son of Sumitrā prepared the funeral pyre according to Rāma’s will.
Then, having slowly circumambulated Rāma with his face turned downward,
Vaidehī approached the blazing fire;
and Maithilī, having bowed down to the deities and the brahmins, [proceeded].
With her hands joined in a gesture of reverence, she spoke thus near the fire:
"As my heart never departs from Rāghava,
so may the Purifier, the witness of the world, protect me on all sides."
Having spoken thus, Vaidehī circumambulated the fire and entered the blazing flame with a heart free from attachment. That vast multitude there, crowded with both young and old, [stood watching].

6.104.026c There he saw Maithilī entering the fire. 6.104.027a As she was entering the fire, a great cry of "Alas! Alas! arose, 6.104.027c among both the Rākṣasas and the Vānaras, resembling a marvel.
Then King Vaiśravaṇa, Yama the subduer of enemies, the thousand-eyed Mahendra, Varuṇa the scorcher of foes,
and the illustrious Mahādeva, the bull-bannered one with three eyes, [arrived].
6.105.002c Brahmā, the creator of the entire world and the best among those who know the Veda,
[spoke]. 6.105.003a All these [gods], having assembled together in celestial chariots as radiant as the sun, 6.105.003c arrived at the city of Laṅkā and approached Rāghava.
Then, raising their massive arms adorned with bracelets,
the best of the gods spoke to Rāghava as he stood with palms joined in reverence:
"You are the creator of the entire world, the most excellent among those possessed of wisdom."
6.105.005c How can you disregard Sītā as she falls into the fire?
6.105.005e How do you not recognize yourself as the foremost among the hosts of gods? 6.105.006a You were formerly Ṛtadhāman, Vasu, and the progenitor of the Vasus.
For you are the original creator and the self-sovereign lord of the three worlds;
you are the eighth among the Rudras and the fifth among the Sādhyas;
the two Aśvins are your ears, and the moon and sun are your eyes.
"O scorcher of enemies, you are seen at both the beginning and the end of the worlds;
yet you disregard Vaidehī like an ordinary mortal man.
Thus addressed by those guardians of the world, Rāghava, the lord of the world, [replied].
6.105.009 Rāma, the best among the upholders of dharma, spoke to the foremost of the thirty gods:
6.105.010 “I consider myself a human, Rāma, the son of Daśaratha.
6.105.010c Who I am, whose I am, and from whence I come—may the Blessed One tell me that.”
To the descendant of Kakutstha who was speaking thus, Brahmā, the best among the knowers of Brahman, said:
"Listen to my truth, O Rāma of true prowess!
You are the divine Nārāyaṇa, the glorious, omnipresent Lord whose weapon is the discus."

You are the single-horned boar, the conqueror of enemies past and future; you are the imperishable Brahman and the truth, O Rāghava, both in the midst and at the end. You are the supreme dharma of the worlds, Viṣvaksena, the four-armed one.
Śārṅgadhanvan, Hṛṣīkeśa, Puruṣa, Puruṣottama, Ajita, Khaḍgadhṛk, Viṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa, and Bṛhadbala—
you are the leader of armies, the leader of the community, as well as intelligence, existence, forbearance, and self-restraint.
You are the source and the dissolution; you are Upendra, the slayer of Madhu. You are Indra in action, the Great Indra; you are Padmanābha, the end-maker of battle.
The divine great seers declare you to be the worthy refuge and the protection itself.
With a thousand horns, the soul of the Vedas, a hundred tongues, and the great bull, you are the sacrifice, you are the *vaṣaṭ* call, and you are the *oṃ* syllable, O scorcher of the foe.
Neither your origin nor your end is known; who indeed are you?
You are seen in all beings, in Brāhmaṇas, and in cows;
in all directions, in the sky, in mountains, and in forests.
You are the glorious one with a thousand feet, a hundred heads, and a thousand supports.
6.105.020a You sustain all beings and the earth together with its mountains;
6.105.020c At the end of the earth, you are seen as a great serpent in the waters. 6.105.021a O Rāma, you support the three worlds, including the gods, gandharvas, and dānavas.
"O Rāma, I am your heart; the goddess Sarasvatī is your tongue.
O Lord, the gods were fashioned as the hairs upon your limbs by Brahmā.
Your closing of the eyes became night, and your opening of the eyes became day."
The Vedas were your refined compositions; there is nothing that exists apart from you.
The entire world is your body, and the surface of the earth is your stability. O one marked with the *śrīvatsa*, fire is your wrath and the moon is your grace.
In ancient times, you traversed the three worlds with your three strides;
having bound the great asura Bali, you made Mahendra the king.
Sītā is Lakṣmī, and you are the god Viṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa, and Prajāpati.

"Having entered a human body for the purpose of slaying Rāvaṇa here, this task of ours has been accomplished by you, O best among the upholders of dharma. Rāvaṇa has been slain; O Rāma, ascend joyfully to heaven."

6.105.027c Your strength and heroism are never in vain; your prowess is never fruitless. 6.105.028a Those men who are devoted shall find their devotion to be fruitful. 6.105.028c Those who are steadfastly devoted to you, the God, the Ancient One, the Supreme Person.
6.105.029a Those men who shall proclaim this shall suffer no defeat. 6.106.001a Having heard these auspicious words uttered by the Grandfather (Brahmā),
Vibhāvasu (Agni) rose up, taking the princess of Videha upon his lap.
Resembling the rising sun, adorned with ornaments of refined gold,
wearing red garments, that young woman had dark, curly hair;
she was of such a form, wise, and possessed of unfading garlands and ornaments.
6.106.003c Taking Vaidehī upon his lap, the Fire-god gave her back to Rāma.
6.106.004a And then Pāvaka, the witness of the world, spoke to Rāma:
6.106.004c “O Rāma, this is your Vaidehī; no sin is found in her.”
Neither by word nor by mind, nor by thought nor by sight did she, being well-conducted and proud of her virtuous character, ever transgress against you;
yet she has been carried away by Rāvaṇa, a Rakṣasa arrogant in his prowess.
Separated from you, miserable and helpless, I have been driven from the desolate forest;
confined and guarded within the inner apartments, my mind fixed on you and devoted solely to you,
I am protected by throngs of hideous and terrifying-looking ogresses.
Though she was enticed in various ways and even threatened, Maithilī did not give it a thought, for her inner self was fixed upon you;
O Rāghava, accept her, who is pure in nature and free from sin.
"Nothing at all need be said; I command you.
Thus addressed, the immensely radiant Rāma, steadfast and of firm prowess—the best among the upholders of dharma—spoke to the foremost of the thirty gods.
6.106.011a Sītā certainly deserves purification in the three worlds;
6.106.011c for this auspicious woman has dwelt for a long time in Rāvaṇa’s inner apartments.
6.106.012a Truly, Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, is a fool, his soul possessed by lust.
6.106.012c Thus the virtuous will speak to me, for they have not cleared Janaki’s innocence;
6.106.013a Her whose heart was devoted to no other, who was my devotee, and who protected my mind—
6.106.013c I too understand Maithili, the daughter of Janaka.
For the sake of convincing the three worlds, I, who rely upon truth,
remained indifferent even as Vaidehī entered the fire;
yet this large-eyed woman has been protected by her own splendor.
Rāvaṇa could not overstep her, just as the great ocean cannot overstep its shore.
For that evil-minded one was not able even in his mind to violate Maithilī,
who was like an unapproachable, blazing crest of fire.
This auspicious woman does not deserve to dwell in the inner apartments of Rāvaṇa;
for Sītā is inseparable from me, just as radiance is from the sun. Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, is pure throughout the three worlds.
For this fame cannot be abandoned by one who possesses self-control, just as [one cannot abandon] the self;
and I must certainly carry out the beneficial words of you all, who are affectionate and honored by the world, as you speak thus for my welfare.
Having spoken these words,
the mighty Rāma, being praised by those of great strength for his own deed, was reunited with his beloved.
Rāghava, who was worthy of happiness, experienced that bliss.
Having heard these auspicious words well-spoken by Rāghava,
Maheśvara uttered this even more auspicious speech:
"O lotus-eyed one, O mighty-armed one, O broad-chested scorcher of foes!
By good fortune, O best of weapon-bearers, this deed has been accomplished by you.
By good fortune, the terrible darkness that had increased over the entire world [has been dispelled]."
6.107.003c O Rāma, by you the fear born of Rāvaṇa has been turned back in battle. 6.107.004a Having comforted the dejected Bharata and the illustrious Kausalyā,
6.107.004c and having seen Kaikeyī and Sumitrā, the mother of Lakṣmaṇa.
Having obtained the kingdom in Ayodhyā and brought joy to his friends,
O mighty one, having established the lineage in the family of the Ikṣvākus,
and having performed the horse sacrifice and attained unsurpassed fame;

"Having given wealth to the Brahmins, you ought to go to the third heaven. O Kakutstha, here is your father, King Daśaratha, seated upon his celestial chariot; he was your highly illustrious guru in the world of men."
"The illustrious one has gone to the world of Indra, delivered by you as his son;
together with your brother Lakṣmaṇa, pay him your respects. Having heard the words of Mahādeva, the descendant of Kakutstha, along with Lakṣmaṇa, [did so].
Standing upon the peak of the celestial chariot, the lord beheld his father,
who was shining with his own splendor and wearing stainless garments,
together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa; he offered his salutation to him.
6.107.011a Overcome with great joy, the lord of the earth, seated in his celestial chariot,
6.107.011c beheld his son, who was dearer to him than life itself;
then the mighty-armed lord, seated upon his excellent throne, 6.107.012a lifted him onto his lap.
Embracing him with both arms, he then spoke these words:
"O Rāma, heaven itself is not highly esteemed by me, nor the honor shown by the celestial sages;
deprived of you, O Rāma, I tell you this as the truth."
"O best among speakers, those words spoken by Kaikeyī for the purpose of your exile remain fixed in my heart. But now,
having seen you safe and sound, along with Lakṣmaṇa, and having embraced you..."
"Today I am liberated from sorrow, like the sun released from mist.
I have been rescued by you, my son— a high-souled and virtuous son—
just as the righteous Brahmin was rescued by Aṣṭāvakra."
"And now I understand, O gentle one, how that Supreme Person was ordained here by the lords of the gods for the purpose of slaying Rāvaṇa.
Kausalyā has indeed achieved her purpose, O Rāma, who has you returned home."

6.107.018c O slayer of enemies, she will joyfully behold you returned from the forest. 6.107.019a Truly successful are those men, O Rāma, who shall see you, the lord of the earth, returned to the city, wet with water and consecrated.
"O gentle one, by you— who are devoted, powerful, pure, and a follower of dharma— I wish to see you reunited with Bharata.
Fourteen years have been spent by you in the forest."
6.107.021c Having dwelt together with Sītā and the wise Lakṣmaṇa,
6.107.022a you have completed your forest exile and fulfilled your vow;
6.107.022c having slain Rāvaṇa in battle, the gods have been gratified by you.
"O slayer of enemies, you have accomplished your task and attained glorious renown;
established in the kingdom with your brothers, may you attain a long life.
To the king who was speaking thus, Rāma replied with palms joined in reverence:
6.107.024c O knower of dharma, show favor toward Kaikeyī and Bharata.
6.107.025a When you said to Kaikeyī, "I abandon you along with your son," 6.107.025c may that terrible curse not touch Kaikeyī and her son, O Lord.
6.107.026a Having said "So be it" to Rāma, who stood with palms joined in reverence, and having embraced Lakṣmaṇa, the great king spoke these words again:
6.107.027a "Serve Rāma with devotion, together with Vaidehī Sītā."
Great joy has been produced for me, and you have obtained the fruit of dharma.
O knower of dharma, you shall attain dharma and vast fame upon this earth;
and when Rāma is pleased, you shall likewise attain heaven and great majesty.
"Serve Rāma— blessings be upon you, O increaser of Sumitrā’s joy—
for Rāma is always devoted to the welfare of the entire world.
These three worlds, along with Indra, the Siddhas, and the supreme ṛṣis [rely upon him]."
Having approached that Great-Souled One, they worship the Supreme Person.
This is that which has been described as the unmanifest, the imperishable, created by Brahman—
the secret heart of the gods, O gentle one, [revealed by] Rāma, the scorcher of foes.
"By serving Rāma with devotion, together with Vaidehī Sītā, you have attained the practice of dharma and vast renown.
Having spoken thus to Lakṣmaṇa, who stood with palms joined in reverence, the mighty-armed one—
The righteous king spoke these auspicious words to Vaidehī:
"O Vaidehī, you should not harbor anger regarding this abandonment;
this was done by Rāma, who desires your welfare, for the sake of proving your purity."
"O fair-browed one, you need not be instructed regarding service to your husband;
however, I must certainly say this to you: he is your supreme deity.
Having thus instructed his two sons as well as his daughter-in-law Sītā, [he departed].
6.107.036c Blazing with splendor, Daśaratha traveled to the world of Indra by means of a celestial chariot.
6.108.001a When the descendant of Kakutstha had departed, Mahendra, the subduer of Pāka,
being exceedingly pleased, spoke to Rāghava as he stood with palms joined in reverence.
"O Rāma, scorcher of enemies, the sight of you has not been in vain for us. I am filled with joy because of this; therefore, speak whatever you desire in your mind.
Thus addressed, the descendant of Kakutstha replied with palms joined in reverence.
6.108.003c Together with my brother Lakṣmaṇa and my wife Sītā, 6.108.004a if affection has arisen for me, O Lord of all the gods,
6.108.004c I shall speak; grant my word its fulfillment, O best among those who speak truth.
"May all those monkeys who have gone to the abode of Yama, having exerted their prowess for my sake, regain their lives and rise up.
Devoted to what is dear to me, they do not even count the cost of death."

"By your grace, may they be reunited; this is the boon I choose. O giver of honor, I wish to see those golāṅgūlas and bears free from disease, free from wounds, and endowed with strength and prowess."
"Even out of season, choice roots and fruits,
as well as pure rivers, shall be present wherever the monkeys stay.
Having heard these words of the high-souled Rāghava, [he departed].
6.108.009 Mahendra replied with these words, which were indicative of his pleasure:
6.108.010a “O dear one, O delight of the Raghus, this boon you have requested is indeed great.
6.108.010c The monkeys shall arise like those who have been asleep at the end of their slumber.”
6.108.011 With friends, kinsmen, relatives, and their own people,
they shall all come together, joined with supreme joy. 6.108.012 Out of season, the trees will be variegated with flowers and laden with fruit.
"O great archer, there will be rivers filled with water. With their limbs first covered in wounds and then again free of wounds,
all the monkeys became astonished, wondering, 'What is this?'"
6.108.014 Seeing the descendant of Kakutstha, whose purpose was fully accomplished, all the foremost of the gods first offered praise to him who is worthy of praise, together with Lakṣmaṇa, and said:
6.108.015 "Go from here to Ayodhyā, O hero, and dismiss the monkeys."
"Console this Maithilī, who is devoted to you and has undergone such hardship. Look upon your brother Bharata, who observes vows out of grief for you;
go and have yourself consecrated, and bring joy to the citizens."
Having spoken thus and taken leave of Rāma along with the son of Sumitrā,
the gods, joyful, ascended to heaven in celestial chariots resplendent as the sun.
And the descendant of Kakutstha paid homage to all those foremost of the thirty deities.
Then, together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, he ordered them to take up residence there.
Thereupon, that illustrious and vast army, protected by Lakṣmaṇa and Rāma, was filled with joyful people.
Blazing with splendor, she shone forth in every direction,
like the night presided over by the cool-rayed moon.
When that night had passed, Rāma, the subduer of enemies, arose comfortably from his rest.
6.109.001 Having asked after his victory, Vibhīṣaṇa, with palms joined in reverence, spoke these words:
6.109.002 “Baths, body-unguents, garments, and ornaments;
divine sandalwood pastes and various kinds of garlands.”
"Moreover, O Raghava, these women, experts in ornamentation and with eyes like lotuses, have arrived and will bathe you according to the prescribed rites.
Thus addressed, the descendant of Kakutstha replied to Vibhishana.
"Invite those monkeys, headed by Sugrīva, to a bath. For on my account, that righteous prince— tender-limbed, mighty-armed, and true to his word— is suffering, though he is accustomed to comfort."
"Without that son of Kaikeyī, Bharata, who walks the path of dharma,
bathing, fine garments, and ornaments hold no value for me.
Let us return quickly to that city by this very same path."
"For this path leading to Ayodhyā is indeed extremely difficult to traverse.
Thus addressed, Vibhīṣaṇa replied to the descendant of Kakutstha:
"O prince, I shall cause you to reach that city within a single day."

"May you be blessed; this celestial chariot named Puṣpaka, which resembles the sun, belonged to my brother Kubera, but was seized by force from him by Rāvaṇa. That very chariot, resembling a cloud, stands here."
"By means of that vehicle you shall go to Ayodhyā, O elephant-like one.
If I am worthy of your favor, and if you remember my virtues,
then stay here for a while, O wise one, if you have any affection for me."

"O Rāma, together with your brother Lakṣmaṇa and your wife Vaidehī, you shall be honored with all desired objects, and only then will you depart. O Rāma, may you remain full of affection for me, along with your army and your circle of friends."
"O Raghava, accept this hospitality prepared by me, offered out of affection, great respect, and friendship. I am your servant;
I am indeed not commanding you."
6.109.015a Thus addressed, Rāma then replied to Vibhīṣaṇa,
6.109.015c while all the rākṣasas, the vānaras, and everyone else were listening.
6.109.016a "O hero, O scorcher of foes, I have been honored by you with this counsel."
"With all my soul, through my actions, and with the highest friendship,
I would certainly not fail to carry out your command, O Lord of Rākṣasas;
yet my mind hastens to see my brother Bharata."
He who came to Citrakūṭa to turn me back—
his word was not heeded by me even as he entreated with his head bowed in supplication;
[he who came] to Kausalyā, Sumitrā, and the illustrious Kaikeyī.
"O Lord of the Rākṣasas, quickly bring before me my elders, my friends, and the citizens along with their sons;
for once my task is accomplished, staying here will no longer be acceptable to me."
"O gentle Vibhīṣaṇa, grant me leave; I have been honored by you. You should certainly not feel resentment; I take my leave of you with haste.
Then [he beheld] that [palace] with its golden, variegated walls and its pedestals of lapis lazuli and gems.
Surrounded on all sides by gabled chambers with the luster of silver,
it was adorned with white banners and flags;
it was beautified by golden mansions and decorated with golden lotuses.
It was strewn with networks of tiny bells, adorned with windows of pearls and gems,
and encircled on all sides by clusters of bells that produced sweet sounds;
shaped like the peak of Mount Meru, it had been constructed by Viśvakarman.
Adorned with many palatial mansions resembling pearls and silver,
it was furnished with floors variegated with crystal and with excellent seats made of lapis lazuli, provided with costly coverings and endowed with great wealth.
Having presented that unassailable, mind-swift celestial chariot which had arrived,
Vibhīṣaṇa stood there before Rāma.
Then, seeing that Puṣpaka, adorned with flowers, standing before him...
6.110.001 Standing nearby, Vibhīṣaṇa replied to Rāma.
6.110.002 With palms joined in reverence, bowing low and humble, that lord of the rākṣasas,
filled with haste, said to the descendant of Raghu, "What shall I do?"
6.110.003 With great splendor, Rāghava, having reflected, spoke these words imbued with affection while Lakṣmaṇa listened:
6.110.004 "O Vibhīṣaṇa, the forest-dwellers have exerted themselves in their endeavors."
"Honor [him] with jewels, various riches, and ornaments. O Lord of Rākṣasas, Laṅkā has been conquered by these men who,
casting aside the fear for their lives, were joyful and never retreated in battles."
"O giver of honor, when these leaders of the monkey troops— who are worthy of respect— have been thus honored by you, who are grateful, they will be filled with contentment.
[They shall honor] one who is generous, a gatherer of followers, compassionate, and illustrious."
"Since they perceive you as such, for that reason I am awakening you.
Having been addressed thus by Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa honored all those monkeys by distributing precious gifts among them.
Then, seeing those leaders of the yakṣa hosts honored with jewels and wealth,
Rāma ascended that unsurpassed celestial chariot,
taking the illustrious Vaidehī upon his lap as she felt bashful.
6.110.010c Together with his valiant brother Lakṣmaṇa, who was armed with a bow,
6.110.011a Kākutstha, standing upon the celestial chariot, spoke to all the monkeys,
6.110.011c as well as to the highly heroic Sugrīva and the Rākṣasa Vibhīṣaṇa.
"O best of monkeys, this service to a friend has been performed by you. Permitted by me, all of you may now depart as you please.
For that which is the duty of a companion or a well-wishing friend, O scorcher of enemies—"
"O Sugrīva, you who fear unrighteousness, all that has been accomplished by you.
Return quickly to Kiṣkindhā, surrounded by your own army.
O Vibhīṣaṇa, dwell in your own kingdom in Laṅkā, which has been granted to you by me."
"Even the gods, including Indra himself, would not be able to overpower you.
I shall return to Ayodhyā, my father’s capital;
I wish to take my leave of you all and bid you farewell."
Thus addressed by Rāma, those mighty monkeys, as well as the Rākṣasa Vibhīṣaṇa, spoke with palms joined in reverence to Rāma:
"We desire to go to Ayodhyā; may your lordship lead us all there."

"O son of the king, having seen you moist from the consecration and having saluted Kausalyā, we shall return to our own homes before long. Thus addressed by the monkeys along with Vibhīṣaṇa, the righteous-souled one [replied].
The illustrious Rāghava spoke to Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa:
"I have obtained that which is dearer than the dearest, in that I, together with my friends and accompanied by all of you, shall find joy upon returning to the city."
"O Sugrīva, ascend quickly to the celestial chariot along with the monkeys! O Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, you too ascend it together with your ministers.
Then Sugrīva, together with his army, ascended that divine Puṣpaka chariot.
Vibhīṣaṇa, together with his ministers, quickly and swiftly ascended.
Once they had all boarded, that supreme throne of Kubera,
authorized by Rāghava, soared into the sky.
He traveled by means of that radiant celestial chariot yoked with swans;
joyful and confident, Rāma shone like Kubera.
But that unsurpassed celestial chariot was dismissed by Rāma.
6.111.001c He leapt up like a great cloud driven by the wind. 6.111.002a Then, casting his gaze in every direction, Rāma, the joy of the Raghus,
spoke to Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, whose face was like the moon.

6.111.003a Behold, O Vaidehī, Laṅkā situated upon the peak of Trikūṭa, which resembles the summit of Kailāsa and was built by Viśvakarman. 6.111.004a Behold this battlefield, a mire of flesh and blood.
6.111.004c O Sītā, this was the great slaughter of the monkeys and the Rākṣasas.
6.111.005a For your sake, O large-eyed one, Rāvaṇa has been slain by me;
6.111.005c here Kumbhakarṇa has been killed, as well as the night-stalker Prahasta.

6.111.006a Here, Indrajit, the son of Rāvaṇa, was slain in battle by Lakṣmaṇa; 6.111.006c as were the hideous Virūpākṣa, Mahāpārśva, and Mahodara. 6.111.007a Akampana was also slain, along with other powerful Rākṣasas.
6.111.007 Triśiras, Atikāya, Devāntaka, and Narāntaka—
6.111.008 there, his wife named Mandodarī lamented for him,
surrounded by a thousand co-wives who were weeping.
6.111.009a But this sacred ford of the ocean is visible here, O lady of lovely countenance,
6.111.009c where, having crossed the sea, we stayed for that night.
6.111.010a This bridge was built by me across the ocean, that mass of waters.
"O large-eyed lady, for your sake this bridge of Nala was most difficult to construct. Behold, O Vaidehī, the unshakeable ocean, the abode of Varuṇa,
shoreless and roaring, frequented by conchs and shells."
"O Maithilī, behold the golden lord of mountains, Hiraṇyanābha,
which rose up after Hanumān had split the ocean for the sake of rest.
It was here that this King of the Rākṣasas, Vibhīṣaṇa, arrived."
6.111.014a Here is seen that Kiṣkindhā with its variegated forests, O Sītā;
6.111.014c the lovely city of Sugrīva, where Vālin was slain by me.
6.111.015a There he is seen, O Sītā, like a great rain-cloud flashing with lightning.
6.111.015c Ṛśyamūka, the best of mountains, is covered with golden minerals.
6.111.016a It was there that I met with Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys;
6.111.016c and an agreement was made by me, O Sītā, for the purpose of slaying Vālin.
6.111.017a Here is that Pampā lake, with its lotuses and variegated forests,
6.111.017c where, bereft of you, I lamented in great distress.
6.111.018a On its shore, I beheld Śabarī, who practices the dharma.
6.111.018c Here, Yojanabāhu and Kabandha were slain by me.
6.111.019a O Sītā, that majestic lord of the forest is seen here in Janasthāna,
6.111.019c where a great battle took place on your account, O playful lady.
Of the cruel Rāvaṇa and the high-souled Jaṭāyu;
Khara was slain in battle and Dūṣaṇa struck down,
as was the immensely powerful Triśiras, by me with my straight-flying arrows.
6.111.021a Thus the variegated leaf-hut, beautiful to behold, is seen,
6.111.021c where you were forcibly carried away by Rāvaṇa, the lord of the rākṣasas.
6.111.022a This is the lovely Godāvarī, with its clear waters and auspicious nature.
"6.111.022c Indeed, this hermitage of Agastya is visible; look, O Maithilī!

6.111.024a These dwellings of ascetics are visible to you, O slender-waisted one, 6.111.024c where Atri, the head of the community, dwells with a splendor like that of the sun or fire. 6.111.024e Here, Sītā, you saw an ascetic woman practicing her religious duties.
"In this place, the giant-bodied Virādha was slain by me.

where the son of Kaikeyī came to propitiate me."
6.111.027a There is that Yamunā visible in the distance, with its variegated forests;
6.111.027c there, this glorious hermitage of Bharadvāja shines forth.
6.111.028a O lady of excellent complexion, here is seen the Gaṅgā, which flows through the three paths.
6.111.028c And here is Śṛṅgaverapura, where Guha met us.
6.111.029a There is Ayodhyā, the capital city of my father, visible there.
6.111.029c O Vaidehī, having returned, offer your salutations to Ayodhyā once more.
Then all those monkeys and the Rākṣasa Vibhīṣaṇa,
leaping up again and again, beheld that city of auspicious appearance. Then they saw it, garlanded with white palaces.
The monkeys beheld the city of Ayodhyā, with its vast courtyards crowded with elephants and horses,
like Amarāvatī, the city of Mahendra.
When the fourteenth year was complete, on the fifth day, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa reached the hermitage of Bharadvāja; self-restrained, he paid homage to the sage.
Having saluted him, he questioned Bharadvāja, whose wealth is his asceticism.
"O Blessed One, do you hear that the city has abundant food and is free from disease?
Is Bharata devoted to his duties, and are his mothers still living?
Thus addressed by Rāma, the great sage Bharadvāja—
6.112.003c He replied to the best of the Raghus with a smile, appearing joyful:
6.112.004a "Bharata, his body smeared with mud and wearing matted hair, awaits you;
6.112.004c placing your sandals before him, he reports that all is well at home."
Long ago, I saw you entering the great forest clad in bark garments, accompanied by a woman as your third companion; fallen from your kingdom and devoted solely to the desire for dharma,
you were on foot, having renounced all possessions, acting in obedience to your father’s word.
6.112.006c Deprived of the enjoyments of heaven, like a god fallen from heaven,
6.112.007a seeing him thus, O conqueror of assemblies, compassion first arose within me; 6.112.007c for he was devoted to the words of Kaikeyī and subsisted on wild roots and fruits.
6.112.008 Now that you have conquered your enemies and see yourself with your circle of friends and kinsmen so thoroughly prosperous, my joy for you is unsurpassed.
6.112.009 And all of your happiness and sorrow, O Raghava, is known to me.
6.112.009c That which you have obtained in abundance, beginning with the slaughter at Janasthāna; 6.112.010a while you were occupied for the sake of the Brahmin and protecting all the ascetics;
6.112.010c as well as the sighting of Mārīca and the abduction of Sītā.

6.112.011a The sight of Kabandha and likewise the arrival at Pampā; 6.112.011c your friendship with Sugrīva and how Vālī was slain by you; 6.112.012a the search for Vaidehī and the deeds of the son of the Wind-god.
And when Vaidehī was found, the bridge of Nala was constructed;
and how Laṅkā was set ablaze by the joyful leaders of the monkey hosts,
along with his sons, kinsmen, ministers, army, and mounts.
6.112.013c And how Rāvaṇa, that thorn in the side of the gods, was slain in battle;
6.112.014a How you met with the thirty deities, and how the boon was granted to you—
6.112.014c All this is known to me through my ascetic power, O lover of dharma.
"O best among those who wield weapons, I too shall grant you a boon here. Accept this water of honor (arghya); tomorrow you shall depart for Ayodhyā.
Having accepted those words with his head bowed, the prince—
"Very well," he replied, and being greatly delighted, the illustrious one requested this boon:
"O Blessed One, let all the trees along the road as we travel toward Ayodhyā bear fruit out of season and exude honey."
6.112.018a Fruit-bearing trees became fruitless, and those adorned with flowers were flowerless; 6.112.018c Those trees, though possessing full foliage, became dry, yet they continued to exude honey.
6.113.001a But having gazed upon Ayodhyā, Rāghava fell into deep reflection.
Having reflected thus, he then cast his gaze upon the monkeys.
Then the wise and radiant Rāma, desiring to do what was pleasing, spoke to Hanumān, the monkey of swift prowess.
"Go quickly to Ayodhyā, O best of monkeys;
find out whether the people in the royal palace are well. Upon reaching Śṛṅgaverapura, seek out Guha, who dwells in the forest."
"Speak words of welfare on my behalf to the lord of the Niṣādas.
Upon hearing that I am well, healthy, and free from distress,
Guha— my friend who is like my own self— will be filled with joy."
6.113.006 And Guha, the lord of the Niṣādas, will joyfully inform you of the road to Ayodhyā and the news concerning Bharata.
6.113.007 But Bharata must be told by you, in my name, that all is well.
"Tell him that I have accomplished my purpose, along with my wife and Lakṣmaṇa;
tell him of the abduction of Vaidehī by the powerful Rāvaṇa,
my alliance with Sugrīva, and the slaying of Vālī in battle."
6.113.009 And the search for Maithilī, and how she was found by you after crossing the great waters of the imperishable lord of rivers;
6.113.010 the approach to the ocean and the sight of the sea.
6.113.010c And how the bridge was constructed, and how Rāvaṇa was slain;
6.113.011a The granting of boons by Mahendra, Brahmā, and Varuṇa; 6.113.011c And through the grace of Mahādeva, my reunion with my father.
6.113.012 Having conquered the hosts of his enemies and attained unsurpassed glory, the mighty Rāma approaches, his purposes fulfilled, together with his friends.
6.113.013 Having heard this, Bharata then assumed such an expression as befitted the situation.

6.113.013c And you should know all that which concerns me; 6.113.014a all the events and the gestures of Bharata should be understood in their true nature through his facial complexion, his gaze, and his speech.
6.113.015a For whose mind would this ancestral kingdom— not inherited from father or grandfather— not turn, a realm abounding in all desires and teeming with elephants, horses, and chariots?
6.113.016a By chance, the illustrious Bharata might himself become desirous of the kingdom.
"Let the joy of the Raghus rule over the entire earth in its entirety.
O monkey, having ascertained his intention and his resolve,
you ought to return quickly before we have gone too far."
Thus commanded, Hanumān, the son of the Wind-god,
assuming a human form, went swiftly to Ayodhyā.
Having leaped over the path of his father, he passed the auspicious abode of the lord of serpents.
Having crossed the formidable confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā,
and having reached Śṛṅgaverapura and approached Guha,
the valiant Hanumān, delighted, spoke these auspicious words.
"O descendant of Kakutstha, your friend Rāma, whose prowess is truth,
together with Sītā and the son of Sumitrā, has inquired after your welfare.
Having stayed for five nights today according to the word of the sage,"
"Today itself you shall see Rāghava, permitted by Bharadvāja.
Having spoken thus, the one of great splendor, his hair standing on end with joy,
flew up with great speed and momentum, without hesitation.
He beheld Rāmatīrtha and likewise the river Vālukinī;
he saw that Gomatī and also the formidable Sāl forest. Having traveled a long distance, that elephant among monkeys proceeded with haste.

6.113.025c He reached the flowering trees growing near Nandigrāma. 6.113.026a Just one *krośa* from Ayodhyā, he saw Bharata, wearing garments of bark and black antelope skin, dwelling in a hermitage, dejected and emaciated.

6.113.027a He had matted hair, his limbs were smeared with dirt, and he was emaciated by the misfortune of his brother; 6.113.027c he was an ascetic who lived on fruits and roots, self-controlled, and a practitioner of dharma;
6.113.028a he bore a heavy mass of matted locks and was clothed in bark garments and deerskins.
6.113.028c He was self-disciplined, of purified soul, and equal in splendor to a Brahman-sage;
6.113.029a placing those sandals before him, he indeed ruled the earth,
6.113.029c the protector of the world of the four castes from all fears.
He was attended by pure ministers and domestic priests, as well as by army commanders and those clad in saffron robes. Indeed,
they did not recognize him as the prince, for he was dressed in bark and black antelope skin.
6.113.031c The citizens, who are truly devoted to dharma, resolved to liberate him.
6.113.032a To him, who was like Dharma personified and knew what was right, and who was like another Devavanta,
6.113.032c Hanumān, the son of the Wind-god, spoke these words with palms joined in reverence.

"O descendant of Kakutstha, that one whom you grieve for—dwelling in the Daṇḍaka forest, wearing bark garments and matted hair—he has inquired after your welfare. O Lord, I tell you pleasant news: you shall cast off this terrible sorrow."
In this very moment, you shall be reunited with your brother Rāma;
having slain Rāvaṇa and recovered Maithilī, Rāma approaches,
his purpose accomplished, accompanied by his mighty friends.
And the highly energetic Lakṣmaṇa and the illustrious Vaidehī—
Sītā was reunited with Rāma, just as Śacī was with Mahendra.
Having been addressed thus by Hanumān, Bharata, the son of Kaikeyī, [was filled with joy].
6.113.037c He fell down suddenly, and though joyful, he fell into a swoon from that very joy.
6.113.038a Then, rising after a moment and having regained his composure, Rāghava 6.113.038c spoke these words to Hanumān, who speaks so pleasantly: Bharata.
Embracing the monkey with great agitation, the illustrious Bharata, filled with joy, drenched him with abundant teardrops born of his sorrow for Aśoka.
"Are you a god or a human who has come here out of compassion? he asked.
"O gentle one, since you speak pleasant words, I shall give you a pleasant reward:
a hundred thousand cows, a hundred excellent villages,
and sixteen maidens of virtuous conduct, adorned with earrings."
The women were gold-complexioned, with beautiful noses and thighs, and faces as lovely as the moon;
they were adorned with every ornament and distinguished by their noble lineage. Upon hearing of Rāma’s arrival, the prince—
Then, filled with joy at the desire to see Rāma, he was overcome by a wonder comparable to that of the foremost of monkeys;
and out of further delight, he spoke these words.
6.114.001a Many indeed have been the years since my lord departed for the vast forest;
yet I hear this heart-gladdening report concerning his fame. 6.114.002a Ah, this worldly verse that has come to me appears truly auspicious!
6.114.002 Happiness comes even to a man who is still living after a hundred years.
6.114.003 How did the meeting between Rāghava and the monkeys take place?
In what region and by relying on what means did it occur? Tell that to me as I ask you.
Questioned by the prince and seated upon a grass mat,
he then related everything concerning Rāma’s conduct in the forest—
how Rāma had gone into exile after your mother was granted the boon.
Just as King Daśaratha died out of grief for his son,
and just as you were brought swiftly from Rājagṛha by messengers, O Lord,
and how, upon entering Ayodhyā, the kingdom was not desired by you; [all these things have been told].

6.114.007 Having gone to Mount Citrakūṭa, you invited your brother— the crusher of enemies and practitioner of the dharma of the virtuous— to accept the kingdom. 6.114.008 By abiding by the king’s word, he has renounced the sovereignty just as you did.
"Taking up the sandals of the Noble One, you have returned as you were before. O mighty-armed one, all of this is known to you exactly as it happened.
But now, learn from me what occurred after you had departed."
6.114.010 When you had departed, that vast Daṇḍaka forest— where the deer and birds were utterly bewildered— then entered upon its solitude.
6.114.011 As they proceeded through the dense forest, the powerful one went at their head.
6.114.011c Virādha appeared, letting out a most tremendous roar.
6.114.012a Lifting him up— making a great noise, with arms raised and face cast downward—
they threw him into a pit while he was still roaring like an elephant.
Having performed that difficult task, the two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa,
went at evening to the beautiful hermitage of Śarabhaṅga.
When Śarabhaṅga had ascended to heaven, Rāma, whose valor is truth, [remained there].
Having paid homage to all the sages, he returned to Janasthāna. While dwelling there, fourteen thousand Rākṣasas of fearsome deeds were slain by the high-souled descendant of Raghu.
Then Śūrpaṇakhā approached Rāma’s side;
thereupon, commanded by Rāma, the mighty Lakṣmaṇa rose up suddenly,
and seizing his sword, he cut off her ears and nose.
6.114.017c Then, tormented by him, the young woman approached Rāvaṇa.
6.114.018a A terrible Rākṣasa named Mārīca, an attendant of Rāvaṇa,
6.114.018c assumed the form of a jewel-encrusted deer and enticed Vaidehī.
6.114.019a Seeing him, Vaidehī said to Rāma, "Let him be captured!
6.114.019c Oh, what a charming and lovely addition he will be to our hermitage!
6.114.020a Then Rāma, bow in hand, pursued the fleeing creature.
6.114.020c He struck that fleeing deer with a straight-knotted arrow.
6.114.021a Then, when Rāghava had gone after the deer and Lakṣmaṇa had also departed, the gentle Daśagrīva entered the hermitage.

6.114.021e He seized Sītā with force, as a planet seizes Rohiṇī in the sky. 6.114.022a Then, having slain the vulture Jaṭāyu in battle while he was desirous of protecting her, 6.114.022c Rāvaṇa, seizing Sītā, departed swiftly and suddenly.
Then,

standing upon the mountain peak, those monkeys, resembling mountains themselves, were filled with wonder as they beheld Rāvaṇa, the lord of the Rākṣasas, departing while carrying Sītā, appearing truly marvelous.
Then Rāvaṇa, the one who makes the worlds cry out, entered Laṅkā. Having ushered Maithilī into a large, beautiful residence encircled with gold, Rāvaṇa addressed her with conciliatory words.
6.114.026a As he was returning, the descendant of Kakutstha was deeply pained upon seeing the vulture.
6.114.027a Having then cremated the slain vulture, his father’s dear friend, Rāma wandered along the Godāvarī and through the flowering forest regions.
In the great forest, they encountered a *rākṣasa* named Kabandha.
Then, at the word of Kabandha, Rāma, whose prowess is truth,
went to Mount Ṛśyamūka and met with Sugrīva.
6.114.029a A heartfelt affection first arose between the two through their meeting; 6.114.029c through their mutual conversation, their love became deepened.
6.114.030a By the prowess of his own arms, Rāma restored his own kingdom.
Having slain the massive-bodied and mighty Vālin in battle,
Sugrīva was established in the kingdom together with all the monkeys;
he then pledged to Rāma that he would search for the princess.

Commanded by the high-souled Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, ten crores of all those forest-dwellers were dispatched to every direction. While we were lost among them on the Vindhya, the best of mountains—
6.114.033c A great length of time passed for those who were intensely tormented by grief.
6.114.034a But the heroic brother of the king of vultures, named Saṃpāti,
6.114.034c announced the dwelling place of Sītā in the abode of Rāvaṇa.
6.114.035a Thus, dispelling the sorrow of my kinsmen who were overwhelmed by grief,
I exerted my own prowess and leapt across a hundred *yojanas*.
6.114.036a There, I beheld a woman who had gone into an *aśoka* grove.
6.114.036c Seeing her dressed in silk, yet soiled, joyless, and firm in her vows,
6.114.037a having approached that blameless woman and questioned her according to the rules,
6.114.037c and having obtained the jewel as a token of recognition, I have returned with my purpose accomplished.
6.114.038a And having returned once more to Rāma of unwearied deeds, I gave him a token of recognition: that great, radiant jewel.
6.114.039a Upon hearing of Maithilī, he was filled with joy and regained hope for his life.
Having reached the end of his life, like a sick man who has drunk nectar,
he resolved upon the exertion of effort to slay Laṅkā;
desiring to destroy them, he was like the sun wishing to consume all those worlds.
Then, having reached the ocean, he caused Nala to construct a bridge;
by that bridge, the army of the monkey heroes crossed over. Nila slew Prahasta, while Rāghava slew Kumbhakarṇa.
Lakṣmaṇa [confronted] the son of Rāvaṇa, while Rāma himself [confronted] Rāvaṇa. Having met with Śakra, Yama, and Varuṇa,
as well as the celestial sages, that descendant of Kakutstha, the scorcher of his foes, received boons.
Having been granted boons out of affection and having met with the monkeys,
he arrived at Kiṣkindhā by means of the Puṣpaka aerial chariot.
Reaching the Gaṅgā once more, he dwelt there in the presence of the sages.
"Tomorrow, under the conjunction of the Puṣya asterism, you shall see Rāma without obstacle.
Then, having heard those great and truthful words of Hanumān,
Bharata was delighted and joined his palms in reverence.
He spoke these words, gladdening his mind:
"After a long time, my heart's desire has indeed been fulfilled.
Having heard this, Bharata, whose prowess is truth, experienced supreme joy.
6.115.001 Delighted, the slayer of enemy heroes commanded Śatrughna:
6.115.002 "Let pure men worship all the deities and the sacred shrines (*caityas*) of the city with fragrant garlands and musical instruments."
6.115.003a Let the king’s wives, as well as the ministers, the soldiers, and the women of the army,
go forth to behold Rāma’s moon-like face.
6.115.004a Having heard Bharata’s words, Śatrughna, the slayer of enemy heroes—
The valiant one dispatched many thousands of laborers, commanding them:
"Level out the depressions, the uneven places, and the plains;
and let all dwellings beyond this point from Nandigrāma be demolished."
"Let them sprinkle the entire earth with water as cold as ice;
then let others scatter parched grain and flowers from all sides.
And let banners be raised high upon the streets of this most excellent of cities."

6.115.007c And let them beautify the houses until the rising of the sun. 6.115.008a Let hundreds of men scatter along the unobstructed royal road garlands, loose flowers, and fragrant blossoms of five colors.
Accompanied by thousands of rutting elephants adorned with gold, others mounted on female elephants with golden girths,
and great chariot-warriors in their chariots, all set forth with great haste.

Then all the wives of Daśaratha, having mounted their vehicles, set out with Kausalyā at their head, and Sumitrā as well. They went forth to the sound of the horses' hooves and the rattling of the chariot wheels.
6.115.011c By the sound of conchs and drums, the earth seemed to tremble. 6.115.012a And that entire city approached Nandigrāma,
[accompanied] by the foremost of the twice-born, righteous-souled leaders of guilds, and merchants.
Surrounded by ministers holding garlands and sweetmeats in their hands, Bharata— accompanied by the sounding of conchs and kettledrums and praised by bards—
took the feet of his noble elder brother upon his head, he who was skilled in the knowledge of dharma.
Taking a pale white umbrella adorned with white garlands,
and two white yak-tail fans fit for a king and decorated with gold,
he was emaciated from fasting, dejected, and clothed in bark and black antelope skin.
6.115.016a Having heard of his brother’s arrival, he was first filled with joy; 6.115.016c then the high-souled one went out to meet Rāma together with his ministers.
6.115.017a Upon seeing him, Bharata addressed these words to the son of the Wind-god:
"Is it not indeed that the fickle-mindedness of Kapeyi is being indulged?
For I do not see the noble Rama, the descendant of Kakutstha, the scorcher of his foes.
When these words had been spoken, Hanuman replied as follows:
6.115.018c While making his purpose known to Bharata, whose valor is truth, [he said:
6.115.019a "Having reached trees that always bear fruit and flowers, which exude honey,
6.115.019c and which resound with the humming of intoxicated bees— this is by the grace of Bharadvāja."
6.115.020a And this boon was granted to him by Vāsava, O scorcher of foes: 6.115.020c "Hospitality shall be rendered to you and your army, endowed with every excellence.
6.115.021a The terrible roar of the delighted forest-dwellers is now being heard.
"I think that monkey army is crossing the Gomatī river;
behold the shower of dust that has arisen toward Vālukinī. I believe the monkeys are shaking the lovely Sāla grove."
6.115.023a This very thing is seen from afar, spotless and resembling the moon—
6.115.023c the divine Puṣpaka chariot, fashioned by Brahmā with his mind.
6.115.024a Having slain Rāvaṇa along with his kinsmen, it was obtained by the high-souled one.
By the grace of the Giver of Wealth (Kubera), this chariot is divine and as swift as thought.
In it are the two heroic Raghava brothers together with Vaidehi,
as well as the highly effulgent Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa, the lord of the Rākṣasas.
Then a roar, born of joy, reached the heavens,
as women, children, youths, and the elderly cried out, "This is Rāma!
Descending from their chariots, elephants, and horses, they came upon the ground.
6.115.027c The men beheld him seated in the celestial chariot, like the moon in the sky.
6.115.028a With palms joined in reverence, Bharata, filled with joy and looking toward Rāghava,
6.115.028c then honored Rāma with a fitting welcome.
6.115.029a Created by Brahmā through his mind, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa shone in that celestial chariot,
6.115.029c with his broad, long eyes, like another wielder of the thunderbolt.
6.115.030a Then Bharata beheld his brother standing at the front of the chariot.
6.115.030c Bowing down, he paid homage to Rāma, who was like the sun situated upon Mount Meru.
6.115.031a Having been placed upon that celestial chariot, Bharata, whose valor is truth,
6.115.031c approached Rāma and, filled with joy, saluted him once again.

6.115.032a Having raised him up— Bharata, who had been out of his sight for so long— the descendant of Kakutstha, filled with joy, placed him on his lap and embraced him. 6.115.033a Then, having approached Lakṣmaṇa and Vaidehī, that scorcher of foes [greeted them].
Delighted, he offered his salutations and spoke his name, Bharata;
then the son of Kaikeyī embraced Sugrīva, Jāmbavān, and likewise Aṅgada,
as well as Mainda, Dvivida, Nīla, and Ṛṣabha.
6.115.035 Having assumed human form, those monkeys, who were capable of changing their shapes at will,
then joyfully inquired after Bharata’s welfare.
6.115.036 And Bharata, consoling Vibhīṣaṇa, spoke these words:
"By good fortune, with you as my ally, this most difficult task has been accomplished.
Then Śatrughna, having saluted Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa,
subsequently paid homage at Sītā’s feet with humility.
6.115.038a Having approached his mother, who was despondent and emaciated by grief, Rāma bowed down and grasped her feet, seeking to appease his mother’s mind.
6.115.039a He also paid his respects to Sumitrā and the illustrious Kaikeyī.
Then he went to all his mothers and to the family priest.
With palms joined in reverence, all the citizens said to Rāma: "Welcome to you, O mighty-armed one, increaser of Kausalyā’s joy!"
The elder brother of Bharata beheld those thousands of hands raised by the citizens like lotuses emerging from their sheaths. Then Bharata himself took up those two sandals of Rāma.
6.115.042c The knower of dharma joined the feet of the lord of men [to his own].
6.115.043a And then Bharata, with palms joined in reverence, spoke to Rāma:
6.115.043c "O King, this kingdom, which was protected by you, has now been restored to you by me."
Today my birth has become fruitful and my heart's desire has been fulfilled,
since I behold you, the king, returned once more to Ayodhyā.
May your majesty inspect the treasury, the granary, the city, and the army.
"By your splendor, everything has been made tenfold by me.
Seeing Bharata speaking thus, who was so devoted to his brother,
the monkeys and the Rākṣasa Vibhīṣaṇa shed tears.
Then, out of great joy, Rāghava took Bharata onto his lap and,
together with the army, traveled by that celestial chariot to Bharata’s hermitage.
Upon reaching Bharata’s hermitage, Rāghava and his army then [alighted].
Descending from the top of the celestial chariot, he stood upon the surface of the earth.
Then Rāma spoke to that unsurpassed chariot:
"Carry the god Vaiśravaṇa; I give you leave to depart."
Then, permitted by Rāma, that unsurpassed celestial chariot departed toward the northern direction, heading for the abode of the Giver of Wealth.
Rāghava [entrusted it] to his priest, who was equal to himself...
Like Śakra pressing upon the feet of Bṛhaspati, the lord of the immortals, the valiant one sat down together with him on a separate, auspicious seat.
Placing his joined palms to his head, Bharata, the increaser of Kaikeyī’s joy, spoke to his elder brother Rāma, whose prowess is truth:
"My mother has been honored; this kingdom has been granted to me."
6.116.002c Therefore, I give this back to you, just as you gave it to me:
6.116.003a The burden set down by a single, powerful bull; 6.116.003c Like a young colt, I am not able to carry such a heavy load.
Like a dam breached by a great force of water and leaking away,
I consider this unguarded vulnerability in the kingdom to be difficult to repair.
It is like a donkey following the path of a horse, or a crow following that of a swan.
"O God, O subduer of enemies, I do not venture to follow your path.
Just as a tree that has been planted and grown within a dwelling becomes large,
difficult to climb, with a massive trunk and many branches,"
6.116.007a Having blossomed, it might wither away without ever showing its fruits; 6.116.007c he for whose sake it was planted would not experience the benefit thereof.
6.116.008a This is the analogy, O mighty-armed one; you ought to understand its meaning.
6.116.008c O Lord of Men, if you do not indeed govern us, your devoted servants;
6.116.009a then let the world behold you today, consecrated on all sides,
6.116.009c blazing like the sun at midday with radiant splendor.
Awaken and sleep to the sounds of the ensemble of musical instruments, to the tinkling of waist-bands and anklets,
and to the sweet voices of song;
as long as the wheel of sovereignty turns, and as far as the earth extends.
"In the meantime, you must exercise sovereignty over all here.
Having heard Bharata's words, Rāma, the conqueror of enemy cities,
accepted them, saying "So be it," and sat down upon an auspicious seat.
Then, at the command of Śatrughna, skilled barbers—
whose hands were gentle and who worked with great speed— attended upon Rāghava.
However, Bharata and the mighty Lakṣmaṇa had already bathed beforehand.
When Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, and Vibhīṣaṇa, the lord of the Rākṣasas,
had been purified, he— his matted hair cleansed, having bathed, adorned with variegated garlands and ointments,
and clothed in costly garments— stood there, blazing with splendor.
The valiant and illustrious one, the enhancer of the Ikṣvāku dynasty, had Rāma prepared for the occasion; the same was done for Lakṣmaṇa,
and all the wives of Daśaratha performed the preparations for Sītā.
Then those wise women themselves fashioned that heart-stealing ornament;
thereafter, Kausalyā, delighted and affectionate toward her son, took great care to ensure that all the wives of Rāghava were beautifully adorned.
Then, at the word of Śatrughna, the charioteer named Sumantra harnessed and brought forward a chariot beautiful in every part;
seeing that divine chariot standing there, resembling the orb of the sun.
The mighty-armed Rāma, whose prowess is truth, ascended [the chariot]. Meanwhile, the ministers of King Daśaratha in Ayodhyā,
placing the family priest at their head, deliberated purposefully on the matter.

6.116.022a Consulting for the sake of Rāma’s prosperity and for the welfare of the city, 6.116.022c you ought to perform everything that is auspicious for the high-souled Rāma, who is worthy of victory, in preparation for his consecration. 6.116.022e You must do whatever is preceded by rites of blessing for Rāma.
6.116.023 Having thus instructed the family priest, all those ministers set out quickly from the city with the intent of seeing Rāma.
6.116.024 O sinless one, they mounted a chariot yoked with horses, like the thousand-eyed Indra.
6.116.024c Mounting his chariot, Rāma set out for the excellent city. 6.116.025a Bharata took hold of the reins, and Śatrughna took up the parasol.
6.116.025c Lakṣmaṇa fanned him with a whisk above his head.
Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, held a white yak-tail fan,
while Vibhīṣaṇa, the lord of the Rākṣasas, held another that resembled the moon.
At that time, the sky was filled with throngs of ṛṣis, gods, and the hosts of Maruts.
As Rāma was being praised, a sweet sound was heard;
then the immensely radiant Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, mounted the elephant named Śatruñjaya, which resembled a mountain.
6.116.029a Nine thousand monkeys went forth,
having assumed human forms and being adorned with all kinds of ornaments. 6.116.029c With the sounding of conchs and the resonance of kettledrums, they advanced.

6.116.030c Those tigers among men proceeded toward that city garlanded with palaces. 6.116.031a They beheld Rāghava approaching with his attendants, 6.116.031c that great chariot-warrior then shining with a magnificent form upon his chariot.
6.116.032 Having cheered up the descendant of Kakutstha and been greeted in return by Rāma, they followed the high-souled one, who was surrounded by his brothers.
6.116.033 He was likewise encompassed by ministers, brahmins, and the subjects.
Rāma shone with splendor like the moon among the stars.
Surrounded by those who went before him, playing musical instruments and holding cymbals and svastikas in their hands, and joyfully proclaiming auspicious blessings, he proceeded forth.
Unbroken grains of rice, gold, cows, maidens, and likewise twice-born brahmins,
as well as men with sweetmeats in their hands, went before Rāma.
And Rāma [recounted] his friendship with Sugrīva and the prowess of the son of the Wind.
Then he related that deed of the monkeys to his ministers;
and upon hearing it, the inhabitants of the city of Ayodhyā were filled with wonder.
Having told this, the radiant Rāma, surrounded by the monkeys, [proceeded].
He entered Ayodhyā, which was crowded with joyful and well-fed people. Then the citizens raised banners in every house;
he reached his father’s delightful home, inhabited by the descendants of Ikṣvāku.
6.116.039 Having reached and entered the residence of his high-souled father,
he paid homage to Kausalyā, Sumitrā, and Kaikeyī.
6.116.040 Then the prince spoke to Bharata, the best among the righteous.
Then, with a sweet voice, the joy of the Raghus said:
"Inform Sugrīva that my excellent and vast residence, complete with its great Ashoka grove and strewn with pearls and lapis lazuli, is also his."
6.116.042 Having heard those words of his, Bharata, whose valor is truth,
took Sugrīva by the hand and entered that dwelling. 6.116.043 Then [he saw] oil lamps, couches, and coverlets.
6.116.043c Urged on by Śatrughna, they quickly took [the vessels] and entered.
6.116.044a And the highly resplendent younger brother of Rāghava said to Sugrīva:
6.116.044c "O Lord, give orders to the messengers for the consecration of Rāma."

6.116.045a Sugrīva quickly gave four golden jars to the four leaders of the monkeys, 6.116.045c adorned with every kind of jewel, just as at the time of dawn [the waters of] the four oceans [are revealed].
6.116.046a Just as at the time of dawn, [he gave them] from the waters of the four oceans.
"Wait with full jars; act accordingly, O monkeys!
Thus addressed, those high-souled monkeys, resembling elephants, leapt swiftly into the sky like fast-flying Garuḍas.
Jāmbavān, Hanumān, and the monkey Vegadarśin,
as well as Ṛṣabha, then brought jars filled with water;
they carried the water from five hundred rivers in those pitchers.
Then Suṣeṇa, endowed with great strength, brought a jar filled with water from the eastern ocean,
adorned with all kinds of jewels;
and Ṛṣabha quickly fetched water from the southern ocean.
6.116.051 A golden jar filled with red sandalwood and camphor,
6.116.051c Gavaya brought water from the great western ocean;
6.116.052a With a great vessel of jewels, he whose prowess was like the wind brought cool water.
6.116.052c And with the speed of Garuḍa and the wind, he quickly brought water from the north.
6.116.053a For the consecration of Rāma, Śatrughna, together with his ministers,
6.116.053c announced it to the preeminent family priest and to his friends.
Then the aged Vasiṣṭha, purified and accompanied by the brahmins,
seated Rāma— who was already seated upon a gem-studded throne— along with his brother.
Vasiṣṭha, Vāmadeva, Jābāli, and Kāśyapa [sat there].
Kātyāyana, Suyajña, Gautama,
and likewise Vijaya consecrated that tiger among men with clear, fragrant water,
just as the Vasus did for the thousand-eyed Vāsava.

6.116.057a First, they were consecrated by the officiating priests, the Brahmins, as well as by the maidens and the ministers; 6.116.057c and by the warriors, together with the merchants, all being greatly delighted.
6.116.058a And also by the juices of all medicinal herbs, while the deities remained stationed in the sky.
Accompanied by all four world-protectors and all the assembled gods,
Śatrughna held his bright white umbrella,
and Sugrīva, the lord of the monkeys, held a white yak-tail fan.
Furthermore, Vibhīṣaṇa, the lord of the rākṣasas, gave to Rāghava a golden garland, radiant as the moon, blazing with its form, and adorned with a hundred lotuses;
it was presented by Vāyu, impelled by Vāsava.

6.116.061a Endowed with every kind of jewel and adorned with precious gems, 6.116.061c he gave a pearl necklace to the lord of men, impelled by Śakra. 6.116.062a The divine Gandharvas sang and the throngs of Apsarases danced.
At that time, during the consecration of the wise Rāma who was worthy of it,
the earth was rich with crops, the trees were laden with fruit,
and the flowers were fragrant during the festival for the descendant of Raghu.

6.116.064a He gave a hundred thousand horses and likewise cows; 6.116.064c that bull among men first gave a hundred bulls to the twice-born. 6.116.065a Furthermore, he gave thirty crores of gold to the Brāhmaṇas.
Rāghava gave to Sugrīva various ornaments and highly precious garments, as well as a divine garland made of gold and set with jewels, which resembled the rays of the sun, O bull among men.
Upon a seat variegated with lapis lazuli gems and adorned with diamonds and jewels,
the steadfast one gave armlets to Aṅgada, the son of Vālin;
he also gave him an unsurpassed pearl necklace set with the finest gems.
Rāma gave to Sītā two divine, stainless garments and auspicious ornaments, radiant as the rays of the moon. Looking upon them, Vaidehī gave them to the son of the Wind.
6.116.070a Having unfastened the necklace from her own neck, the daughter of Janaka 6.116.070c gazed repeatedly at all the monkeys and at her husband.
6.116.071a Observing her, he who understood gestures spoke to the daughter of Janaka.
"O fortunate one, O beautiful lady, give the necklace to him with whom you are pleased—
him in whom manliness, prowess, and intelligence are ever present.
Then that dark-eyed woman gave the necklace to the son of Vāyu.
6.116.073 With that necklace, Hanumān, the bull among monkeys,
shone like a mountain with a white cloud, pale as a mass of moonbeams.
6.116.074 Then, O scorcher of foes, [the king] gave it to Dvivida, Mainda, and Nīla.
Having beheld all the objects of desire, the lord of the earth bestowed them [upon him].
And all the elder monkeys, as well as the other lords of the monkeys,
were honored with garments and ornaments according to their merit.
Having been honored as was fitting with abundant desires and jewels,
they all departed as they had come, their minds filled with great joy.
Then the most noble Rāghava, with supreme delight, gave his commands.
6.116.077c Rāma, who is devoted to dharma, spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, who knows dharma:
6.116.078a "O knower of dharma, mount this earth along with me, together with my army— this earth formerly inhabited by previous kings."
"You have been raised by my fathers as their equal; therefore, bear the burden of the office of crown prince. Though entreated with all my soul,"
When the son of Sumitrā did not accept the appointment to the position of heir apparent on earth,
the high-souled one then consecrated Bharata.
And Rāghava, whose soul is dharma, having obtained that unsurpassed kingdom,
performed various kinds of sacrifices together with his friends, brothers, and kinsmen—
specifically the Pauṇḍarīka, the Aśvamedha, and the Vājapeya, repeatedly.

And that bull among kings performed various other sacrifices as well. Having obtained the kingdom for ten thousand years, Rāghava performed a hundred horse-sacrifices with excellent horses and abundant sacrificial fees.
With arms reaching down to his knees, broad-shouldered and majestic,
Rāma, followed by Lakṣmaṇa, protected the earth. No widows lamented, nor was there any fear caused by predatory beasts.

6.116.084c Nor was there any fear born of disease while Rāma governed the kingdom. 6.116.085a The world was free from robbers, and no misfortune touched anyone. 6.116.085c Furthermore, the elderly did not have to perform funeral rites for children.

6.116.086 All were indeed joyful; everyone became devoted to dharma. Beholding only Rāma, they did not harm one another. 6.116.087 They lived for thousands of years, and likewise, they possessed thousands of sons.
While Rāma ruled the kingdom, people were free from disease and sorrow.
The trees, with their wide-spreading trunks, bore flowers and fruit perpetually;
the rain-cloud poured forth at the proper season, and the wind was pleasant to the touch.

Content with their own respective duties, they engaged in their own works; while Rāma governed, the subjects were devoted to dharma and free from falsehood. All were endowed with auspicious marks, and all were dedicated to righteousness.
Rāma ruled the kingdom for ten thousand years.
